home-affordability-calculator.assumptionNote: Uses the 28/36 rule common in US mortgage lending. Property tax and homeowner's insurance are excluded, so they reduce how much house the payment actually covers.
benefits: Get a realistic price ceiling before you fall in love with a listing.
See which rule limits you: the housing ratio or your existing debts.
Test how paying down debt or saving a bigger down payment changes your budget.
Free, instant, and private - no pre-approval paperwork needed.

faqs.a: Lenders use two caps: housing costs should be at most 28% of gross monthly income, and all debts including housing at most 36%. Your maximum payment is the lower of the two. So on $10,000/month income with $500 of debts, the caps are $2,800 and $3,100 - the $2,800 housing cap wins.
Debts eat the 36% side of the rule. Every $500 of monthly debt cuts roughly $80,000-$100,000 off your affordable price at typical rates, because the debt cap becomes the binding limit.
faqs.q: How do my debts affect affordability?

faqs.a: Both help, but a bigger down payment raises the price ceiling dollar-for-dollar, while paying down debt can raise it more if debts are the binding limit. Test both in the calculator to see which moves your number further.
faqs.q: Bigger down payment or paying off debt first?

faqs.a: No - and that is the honest catch. Property tax and insurance can add 20-40% on top of principal and interest. This calculator gives the price before those costs, so treat it as the ceiling, not the exact budget.
faqs.q: Does this include property tax and insurance?

faqs.a: Roughly 20% of the home price is the classic advice, because it avoids mortgage insurance (PMI) on conventional loans. Less is fine with FHA (3.5%) or other programs, but 20% also lowers your monthly payment directly.
faqs.q: How much down payment do I need?

faqs.a: It is a planning estimate based on the industry-standard 28/36 rule, not a lender's approval. Lenders weigh credit score, employment history, and more. Use this to set your search budget, then get pre-approved for the real number.
faqs.q: Is this the same as pre-approval?

home-affordability-calculator.formula:
Monthly income = annual income / 12
Housing cap = 28% x monthly income
Debt cap = 36% x monthly income - monthly debts
Max payment = min(housing cap, debt cap)
Max loan = max payment / (r / (1 - (1+r)^-n)), r = rate/12, n = years x 12
Affordable price = max loan + down payment
howTo: Enter your gross annual household income.
Enter your total monthly debt payments (car loans, cards, student loans).
Enter the mortgage rate and term you expect.
Read your affordable price, max payment, max loan, and which rule limits you.
keyFacts: The 28/36 rule is the industry standard for how much house income can support.
Housing costs should be at most 28% of gross monthly income.
All debts including housing should be at most 36%.
The lower of the two caps sets your maximum payment.
Property tax and insurance are extra - this price is before them.

howcalc.heading: How we calculate
howcalc.s1: The 28% rule caps housing at 28% of gross monthly income.
howcalc.s2: The 36% rule caps all debt (housing + other) at 36% of income; the lower of the two wins.
